architecture_review:
### Atomic source capture and durable publication

`LmdbSailStore.prepareBackupStage()` prepares a stage before commit. `TripleStore.writeBackupBoundary()` checks its transaction number, predecessor boundary, UUID, and record count, then calls `LmdbBackupOutbox.write()` using the same native transaction that mutates the RDF statement indexes. Committing the triples transaction therefore commits its recoverable backup source atomically. Aborting that native transaction rolls back both together. The separate value dictionary retains the store's existing paired commit ordering; this change does not claim a single LMDB transaction across both environments.

Sources: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbSailStore.java` — `prepareBackupStage()`, `publishCommittedDelta()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/TripleStore.java` — `writeBackupBoundary()`.

Enabled journaling forces synchronous commits in both native environments, including when the general `forceSync` setting is false. The dictionary commits before triples. `syncBackupPublicationBoundary()` crosses the sink gate to observe that completed boundary; it avoids forcing the same pages again. Publication also waits for the owning source scope to release, including scopes containing physical checkpoints. Startup recovery separately synchronizes historical external stages.

Sources: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/ValueStore.java` and `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/TripleStore.java` — constructors and native environment flags; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbSailStore.java` — `syncBackupPublicationBoundary()`.

The worker publishes contiguous batches of up to 256 stages through `onCommitBatch()`. `LmdbBackupJournal.append()` commits the batch and its head together in a separate archive LMDB environment using synchronous commit flags. Acknowledgement advances only after that succeeds. If the process stops between archive commit and acknowledgement, replay checks existing archived bytes and predecessor identities. Legacy external-stage deletion first checkpoints a durable file acknowledgement. The optimization removes repeated file creation, synchronization, and model conversion while retaining the source-to-archive durability ordering.

Sources: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/PostCommitBackupPublisher.java` — `publish()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupServiceImpl.java` — `onCommitBatch()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupJournal.java` — constructor, `append()`, `appendStage()`.

### Identity and reclamation

Every prepared stage receives fresh UUID entropy, including attempts later abandoned. A retry may reuse a logical transaction number, but it cannot inherit the aborted attempt's stage identity. Stage headers, predecessor links, committed notifications, archive heads, and acknowledgements carry the identity alongside the transaction number. `nextIdentity()` batches entropy acquisition without reusing identities.

Source: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/PostCommitBackupPublisher.java` — `prepare()`, `nextIdentity()`, `committed()`, `readStage()`.

Reclamation requires an archive-durable acknowledgement tuple captured coherently for the current writer attempt. `writeBackupAcknowledgement()` validates and persists its identity-aware proof in the same native transaction as deletion. Concurrent publication cannot enlarge that transaction's deletion horizon after an older proof was written. Replacement writes retain the new source; maintenance without replacement retains the authoritative current head. Packed cleanup validates checksums, ordering, and range boundaries, and deletes only fully acknowledged packs. Reclaim watermarks become committed only after native success, so rollback and map-growth replay cannot skip unfinished cleanup. Cleanup work is bounded per attempt.

Sources: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/TripleStore.java` — `writeBackupBoundary()`, `writeBackupAcknowledgement()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupOutbox.java` — `reclaim()`, `reclaimPackedBucket()`, `committed()`.

### Bounded memory and compact native staging

The publisher retains at most 4,096 pending notifications and a 256-stage publication batch. Pending and in-flight owned publication payloads share a 1 MiB budget; the sole source writer can additionally hold one provisional chunk of at most 64 KiB. Overflow falls back to the committed native source. Release bookkeeping retains live source scopes, rather than every checkpoint in a stalled backlog. Unpublished durable history remains on disk: bounded notification memory does not mean discarding transactions or capping recoverable history.

Source: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/PostCommitBackupPublisher.java` — `committed()`, `releasedThrough()`, `readStageForPublication()`, `Stage.openNativeSource()`.

Small complete frames share a reserved MAIN-catalog value. Initialization probes a 960-byte reservation in a nested transaction, with a 640-byte fallback, and accepts only a single-leaf catalog without overflow. Later schema growth triggers atomic evacuation when that condition ceases to hold. The new `R4H2` envelope compresses the existing `R4P1` pack only after its raw representation exceeds the reservation. Decoded size is capped at 1,920 bytes and the native pack limit before allocation. Readers validate lengths, padding, decompression, and the inner pack checksum. Both `R4H1` and `R4H2` remain readable. If compression cannot fit, rollover preserves the complete old pack in the unchanged cold-pack encoding; individual chunk frames and public delta records are unchanged.

Source: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupOutbox.java` — `initializeCatalog()`, `reserveCatalog()`, `catalogFits()`, `tryPutCatalogPack()`, `copyCatalogPack()`, `appendSmallFrame()`.

### Lexical capture and ownership

The removal fast path copies supported dictionary terms directly into the public record encoding while the physical dictionary writer remains admitted. Native buffers and numeric term IDs do not escape into asynchronous backup work. Inline literals and nested triple terms retain the protected model fallback. Literal tags, lengths, language, and datatype validation remain active. Metadata reuse is limited to 32 owned UTF-8 entries of at most 4 KiB each, scoped to an opaque physical-writer identity that changes across rollback and dictionary checkpoints.

Source: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/ValueStore.java` — `writeBackupRecord()`, `NativeBackupWriter`, `backupMetadataFor()`, `NativeBackupMetadataCache`.

`LmdbBackupRecordBuffer` keeps encoded records in memory up to 64 KiB, then spills. Memory snapshots own their bytes; spill snapshots are tied to the buffer generation and reject use after invalidation. `EncodedRecords` lets publication consume existing lexical bytes without decoding RDF models and encoding them again. The empty-string shortcut emits the same zero length as the existing codec.

Sources: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupRecordBuffer.java` — `addNativeStatement()`, `snapshot()`, `clear()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupDeltaCodec.java` — `EncodedRecords`, `writeString()`.

### Historical input, public export, and downgrade limits

The candidate recovers historical UUID-named `R4O1` stage files and file acknowledgements, reads existing public delta logs, and exports native history into the unchanged `txn-*.delta.gz` representation. Public delta versions and record encodings remain supported. Export continuity still requires complete transaction and generation coverage.

Sources: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/PostCommitBackupPublisher.java` — `LegacyRecoveryIndex`, recovery constructor; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupServiceImpl.java` — `exportTransactionLogs()`, `collectRestoreDeltaLogs()`, `validateLogCoverage()`.

Public export compatibility does **not** imply live-store downgrade compatibility. The first enabled open installs new native outbox databases, before any user transaction; disabling journaling does not remove them. Unpatched `8fc7` rejects this schema during ordinary discovery and cached/CLEAN prepared admission. Its `PreparedBulkStore.capture()` still invokes `LegacyStoreDiscovery.validateCurrentMetadata()`, and ordinary discovery also rejects unknown database names. A full native snapshot contains those databases and has the same limitation. These conclusions come from the static downgrade audit; no old-binary restore test was performed.

The old archive reader does not discover `txlog/journal/<generation>`. Missing unexported history fails its coverage check rather than silently restoring an earlier boundary. Rollback therefore needs an old-readable pre-upgrade snapshot plus fully exported compatible history, or a logical migration into a separately created old-format store. Existing store-format and manifest version numbers alone do not express this boundary.

Audit references at baseline `8fc7`: `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/PreparedBulkStore.java` — `readSealed()`, `readCurrent()`, `capture()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LegacyStoreDiscovery.java` — `validateCurrentMetadata()`, `readDatabaseCatalog()`, `validateKnownDatabases()`; `core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbBackupServiceImpl.java` — `collectRestoreDeltaLogs()`, `validateLogCoverage()`.
downgrade_compatibility_static_audit:
# Incremental-backup candidate: downgrade compatibility audit

Static audit against unpatched base `8fc7b0137164ffdc1f5d080b943fd362931137dd` and the integrated candidate. No JVM or old-binary downgrade test was run. Source was read with `git show 8fc7:<path>` in `/workspace/scratch/11cb17cbd1fd/rdf4j`.

## Conclusion

**Normal `LmdbStore` opening with unpatched 8fc7 fails closed once the candidate has installed native backup storage. A cached/prepared/CLEAN manifest does not bypass the old native schema checks.** I found no normal public-API path that admits the changed store with the old stale namespace backup head.

The protection is strict structural admission already present in 8fc7, rather than a new format-version fence. The candidate leaves `LmdbStoreFormat.CURRENT_VERSION` at 7, the prepared certificate version at 1, and `backup-journal.properties` version at 1. Backup metadata still uses the same journal mode and generation fields. Those version fields alone therefore do not describe downgrade compatibility.

Installing the native schema happens while opening a store with backup journaling enabled, before the first user write: the candidate creates the 32 bucket databases and the hot/cold pack database pair. Consequently, the limit is stronger than “do not downgrade after writing a compressed pack.” A first enabled open is enough. Disabling journaling later does not remove those databases and does not restore old-binary compatibility.

## Why the cached-manifest path rejects the store

All paths below are in the unpatched base:

1. `LmdbStore.initializeInternal()` loads properties, validates persisted capabilities, then calls `PreparedBulkStore.read()`. It creates the writable backing store only after prepared admission or ordinary discovery completes.
2. `PreparedBulkStore.read()` tries `readSealed()` and then `readCurrent()`.
3. `readSealed()` parses and checks the certificate, but still calls `capture(directory, properties, config)` before comparing it with the expected snapshot. It does not trust the cached certificate by itself.
4. `readCurrent()` also calls `capture()`.
5. `capture()` opens native read-only transactions, checks the CLEAN marker and exact triple binding, and always calls `LegacyStoreDiscovery.validateCurrentMetadata()`.
6. The old `validateCurrentMetadata()` opens only known contexts, namespaces, and index databases. It requires `databaseEntries(triplesMain) == tripleDatabases.size()`. The candidate's new outbox named databases violate that equality even if the MAIN hot key is absent. The MAIN hot key is an additional unmatched entry when present.
7. Prepared admission catches the resulting failure and returns no prepared snapshot. `LmdbStore.initializeInternal()` then invokes ordinary discovery, which also rejects the added schema. It does not continue into the writable constructor after that failure.

Expected fast-path failure is `Unrecognized entry in current LMDB triple database catalog`; the eventual public diagnostic normally comes from ordinary discovery after prepared admission declines.

## Why ordinary discovery also rejects it

In 8fc7, `LegacyStoreDiscovery.readDatabaseCatalog()` enumerates the printable-ASCII named database interval. Although the binary MAIN hot key falls below this interval during nonexhaustive startup, the `backup-outbox-*` database names are in the interval and are discovered.

The old `validateKnownDatabases()` builds the expected triples set from `contexts`, optional `namespaces`, and valid statement indexes only. It then requires exact set equality and rejects an extra name with `Unrecognized named database in triples environment: ...`. The new bucket/hot/pack databases therefore provide the necessary rejection independently of the hot-envelope version, compressed content, pending backlog, or acknowledgement state. A sufficiently large catalog can instead fail the old fixed catalog cap earlier, which is also rejection.

Additional independent incompatibilities exist:

- Exhaustive discovery starts from the first MAIN key, so it rejects the binary hot value as an unrecognized ordinary record.
- The new `backup-published-acknowledgement` namespace key is absent from the old namespace whitelist. If reached, old namespace validation rejects it.
- The old publisher expects UUID-named external `.stage` files, and its recovery routine verifies the namespace head against the file acknowledgement. It does not know native source buckets or the newer acknowledgement source.

These are actual existing checks, not assumptions that a magic number will eventually fail. The same schema checks apply when the old binary is configured with journaling disabled.

## Why bypassing admission would be unsafe

The candidate's native-staged `TripleStore.writeBackupBoundary()` commits the stage as source authority and returns without updating the old namespace fallback on every user transaction. Current `recoverBackupBoundary()` finds the newest stage across native storage and combines it with that fallback.

The old `TripleStore.recoverBackupBoundary()` reads only `backup-logical-boundary` and `backup-outbox-head` from namespaces. If schema admission were deliberately bypassed, removed, or replaced by a custom internal opener, those values can lag the candidate's actual logical head. That is a concrete reason not to strip the unknown outbox databases or metadata to force a downgrade. Such tampering is outside normal `LmdbStore` behavior; the audited standard paths reject before reaching this interpretation.

This conclusion is scoped to unpatched 8fc7. It does not assert that every historical or custom RDF4J build has the same admission checks.

## Compatibility by artifact

| Item | Candidate reading old data | Unpatched 8fc7 reading candidate data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Historical external R4O1 `.stage` files and file acknowledgement | Supported recovery path | The byte encoding remains recognizable, but new ordinary commits no longer create one external file per transaction |
| Historical public `txn-*.delta.gz` logs | Supported | Public delta versions 1/2/3 and record encoding are unchanged; exported files remain wire-compatible |
| New native source outbox in the live store | N/A | Standard live-store open rejects the additional schema |
| Private archive `txlog/journal/<generation>/data.mdb` | Supported by new journal reader | Not discovered by the old archive reader |
| Explicit new incremental backup artifact | Produced as unchanged public gzip deltas, optionally ZIP-wrapped | Old code can parse these deltas; restoration still requires an old-readable full base and complete compatible generation coverage |
| Full native snapshot made after new backup storage is installed | Supported | Contains the new outbox databases because snapshot copies the native environment; old restored-store admission rejects them |
| Store that never installed native backup storage | Existing formats preserved by this backup change | No new native-outbox downgrade barrier from this change alone |

Public export compatibility is established here by static codec and writer comparison; no cross-binary restore run was performed for this audit.

## Old restore does not silently ignore an unexported suffix

The old `LmdbBackupServiceImpl.listTransactionLogs()` recognizes only top-level `txn-*.delta.gz` files. It does not recursively scan `txlog/journal/<generation>` or interpret the new LMDB archive. Its `collectRestoreDeltaLogs()` combines explicit incremental artifacts with those legacy files, then calls `validateLogCoverage()` before creating the restore destination.

`validateLogCoverage()` validates each predecessor/generation and requires the selected history to end at the requested transaction. If the requested suffix exists only in the new native archive, old restore fails with missing transaction logs instead of returning success at an earlier point. The `verifyBeforeRestore` option does not disable this continuity check.

If the chosen full snapshot itself contains the new native outbox schema, old restore subsequently calls `restored.init()` even for an empty delta list; the standard admission checks reject it before the staging directory is atomically promoted. A checksum-valid full snapshot is not thereby old-runtime compatible.

The practical rollback choices are a pre-upgrade old-readable full snapshot plus fully exported compatible incremental history, or a logical export/import into a separately created old-format store. A new full native backup is not a downgrade conversion. Keep the candidate runtime available to read its private archive and create public incremental artifacts.

## Suggested performance README / final wording

> **Storage compatibility:** This implementation reads historical staged backups and public delta logs, and explicit incremental exports retain the existing gzip delta format. Enabling it installs new native outbox storage and uses a native batch archive under `txlog/journal/<generation>`; unpatched main does not read that private archive. A live store or full native snapshot containing the new outbox schema cannot be opened in place with unpatched main. Disabling journaling does not reverse the storage change. The audited base commit rejects the changed schema during startup, including its cached/CLEAN admission path. Keep a pre-upgrade snapshot for rollback, or export and migrate data with a compatible runtime.

Avoid saying “fully backward compatible” without distinguishing public delta encoding from native live-store/full-snapshot compatibility. The no-silent-open conclusion is a static source finding for base 8fc7, not a downgrade test result.
limits: Two pairs per workload reveal order sensitivity and spread but do not establish a precise confidence bound.
This workload uses bounded insert/remove cycles; fresh-value results are reported as a separate campaign.
Aggregate JIT time is reported for every phase and can remain during measurement; it is not writer stall time.
Only this host, configuration, durability, indexes and native/full-adjacency setup are measured.
All forks are retained; no favorable subset or diagnostic samples are pooled into the result.

The drained metric means durable journal publication plus store shutdown, not an empty cleanup or outbox-reclamation queue. Close may persist cleanup candidates, and outbox reclamation can wait for later writes.
A final_backlog value of zero refers only to publication backlog.
Explicit incremental export, gzip generation, retention work and backup-request I/O are outside this benchmark.

Per-fork validation checks live cardinality, transaction/acknowledgement identity and feature readiness; it does not perform full data-equality or backup restore/replay validation. Those require separate correctness tests.
The five-percent flags describe observed added time per transaction, not a universal overhead guarantee.
